title: W-2 Form

origin.title: Form W-2 example image
origin.clearance_note: An example Form W-2 (2024) image published on the Remote People blog, listed as the W-2 source in the Marketing Document Summary sheet. The form layout is the IRS's, and every value is obvious test data: employee 'John Doe', employer 'Company Inc', a 7-digit 'SSN' (4453453) and an 8-digit 'EIN' (23454535), neither a valid format, and locality 'Test'. Two caveats. The publisher is a blog that made an illustration, not a vendor distributing a specimen for reuse. And the two street addresses use real road names with arbitrary numbers; the employee's pairs a North Carolina road with a California ZIP, but the employer's Saratoga address could not be ruled out as matching a real building. Despite the .avif name, the server returns a JPEG, saved here as .jpg.

notes: Fields chosen by the document owner after the first build: boxes 1, 3, 13, 14 and 19. The first build featured boxes 1, 2, 4 and 6. The owner also asked for box 12c's code 'D' with its amount; it was dropped because the parse loses the box 12 codes (each sits beside a small vertical 'Code' label), so the code extracts as null, and the owner chose not to feature box 12 at all. Box 13 is featured through third_party_sick_pay, which extracts true and has its own tight range covering the label and the ticked box. build_images.py flags it because the word 'True' never appears on the page, which is expected for a checkbox; the crop was checked by eye. statutory_employee and retirement_plan share one range covering both boxes, so either would show two ticks in one crop. Box 16 state wages (120.00) is in the parse but extracts synthesized, with no range.
